results.title: Scientists' personality, values, and well-being - PMC - NIH
results.content: In this study, scientists (*n* = 24) and non-scientist controls (*n* = 26) were assessed with respect to their five-factor personality traits, 10 basic values, and subjective well-being (subjective happiness and sense of purpose in life). Compared with the non-scientist control group and with normative data of laypeople, the scientists consistently exhibited greater openness (i.e., traits related to curiosity and intelligence), self-direction (i.e., values related to the pursuit of curiosity, creativity, and autonomous action), happiness, and sense of purpose in life. Furthermore, the results demonstrated that scientists scored higher on subjective happiness and sense of purpose in life in comparison with the non-scientist control group and the normative data of laypeople. To further understand scientists’ psychological characteristics, future studies should investigate such sub-groups with respect to their personality traits, values, and subjective well-being. The results of this study revealed that scientists, as compared with non-scientists, exhibited a higher degree of openness, self-direction, subjective happiness, and sense of purpose.

results.title: How to create personas based on science that actually work
results.content: Personas are a concrete representation of underlying group personality traits clustered together in an abstract individual so that we may better understand the needs of a particular population segment. It is quite difficult, if not almost impossible, to obtain a personality profile of one s*ingle* individual let alone to create a persona based on not one but *multiple* groups of people. However, the most reliable tend to be the big five personality traits. You can get as deep as you want about your research process by reading studies about for instance eye tracking studies that compare viewing behaviors of extroverts and neurotic people to find out what your audience might be more prone to attend to (i.e., look at) so that you can design better products, or to look at their overarching biologically rooted motivations and preferences to build a persona that is representing a actual person.
